A door to the furnace stands to the north, and an eastern colonnade stretches out, hinting at the nursery's former grandeur. Amongst the items scattered around, I found a worn trowel with its bright edge visibly abraded by use, suggesting previous gardening efforts. I also discovered an interesting, aged ball of twine, furred with the passage of time and likely forgotten, lying on the floor. The scene conjures images of days gone by, hinting at the caretakers who once tended to this place, now only shadows of their labor left behind.

runs.narrative:
Exploring a complex and intriguing environment, my journey started in a distinctly cold and barren section I identified as the 'Nursery,' characterized by empty trays of compost under cracked glass and a lone door leading to warmth in the north. Upon noticing a trowel and twine on the floor, I picked up the twine, symbolizing perhaps a quest for tools to aid my exploration. My journey progressed as I ventured east into a colonnade, feeling the weight of the twine in my hand, a tangible link to the tools left behind. 

Further exploration led me through a broken roofed space — the colonnade — and into the tranquil yet confining space labeled 'Cloche,' where a sunken bed under a hinged pane marked my Northern direction. Noticing a stair going down, my curiosity piqued, I cautiously descended. The Sump greeted me with its brick walls and eerie quietness, holding a solitary dipper on its floor. Picking up the dipper became a symbolic act, perhaps representative of searching for a way out or a new beginning

In the vast quietness of the sump room, I spent my time exploring and trying to find a way out. Initially confused and surrounded by brickwork and a half-full, quiet sump, I first picked up a trowel and examined it, which led me to the discovery of a twine and subsequently to an exploration of the nursery above. There, I took a basket, which turned out to be empty, and then opened a cloche door, revealing stairs down to the north. My journey continued through the colonnade, where I found more items such as a dipper and eventually navigated to the sump room once more, employing various items and reading sections of a manual to escape. Making my way past the clay-filled silence, I finally exited the sump room through the south door and started to ascend the stairs, determined to move further from the confinement. Each step carried me closer to the promise of open spaces beyond the brickwork.

My pursuit of exploration and discovery brought me from the quietude of the colonnade to the foreboding yet intriguing space beneath the cloche. Each action, from picking up the trowel to navigating through the vault's empty drawers, to sifting through the mundane contents of the basket, was a step towards understanding this place's enigma. The dipper in my hand became a symbol of my perseverance amidst the emptiness. Eventually, the path led me south, only to redirect my curiosity westward when confronted with the haunting stillness of the sump. My latest move northward was driven by a persistent urge for thorough exploration, even in the repetitiveness of seeing nothing new.
